references.title: Plato, Republic, Book VII (Internet Classics Archive)
references.support: Benjamin Jowett's translation of Republic Book VII, including the Cave and Socrates' explanation of education, the Good, and the philosopher's return. Passage-level support for the article's primary-text paraphrase; relevant locations include 514a–517a, 518b–d, and 519c–521b. The complete Republic was not read.

references.title: Sean McAleer, “The Allegory of the Cave: Book VII,” Plato’s ‘Republic’: An Introduction
references.support: Scholarly chapter relating the Cave to education and the divided line. Chapter 11 discusses the ascent, education, and political return; it also notes that divisions of the allegory's stages can be interpretively subjective. Relevant chapter passages were read; the full book was not.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Plato’s Myths
references.support: Catalin Partenie's discussion of the Cave at Republic 514a–517a identifies it, strictly speaking, as an analogy rather than a myth. Context for the article's technical classification; it does not establish every detail of the Cave interpretation.

references.title: Eric Brown, “Plato’s Ethics and Politics in The Republic”
references.support: Section 2.3 discusses the philosophers' compulsion to rule and differing explanations of their motives; section 5 addresses controversy over the Republic's political implications. Scholarly context, not a claim of consensus or a replacement for Republic VII.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Plato
references.support: Richard Kraut's entry gives Plato's approximate lifespan and cautions that periodization as a composition chronology is disputed. Broad chronological context only; it does not establish the Republic's precise composition date.
